title: Paloma Top-Up & Bill Pay Order Caps and Duplicate Orders
content:
## Rule

The orders of one customer under Paloma Top-Up & Bill Pay are aggregated **per product** (Paloma Airtime Top-Up, Paloma Data Bundle, Paloma Electricity Token, Paloma Bill Pay Utilities, Paloma Bill Pay Television and Paloma Bill Pay School Fees each counted on its own). For the product ordered:

1. **Orders to one destination.** No more than the product's limit of orders to one destination in a rolling 24 hours, the 24 hours ending at the moment the order is handled.
2. **Orders per customer.** No more than the product's limit of orders per customer in a rolling 30 calendar days, the 30 calendar days ending on the handling date.
3. **Order value per customer.** No more than the product's limit of order value per customer in a rolling 30 calendar days: the US-dollar values of the same orders counted under item 2, totalled.

Each of the three is counted **including the new order** and **excluding orders whose status is cancelled or refunded**. An order over any cap is not placed.

4. **Duplicates.** A second order of the same product, destination and value placed within the product's duplicate window (in hours) of the first is treated as a duplicate and not placed. The first order is one of the customer's own orders whose status is submitted, processing or delivered.

The counts, the values, the destinations and the order moments are taken from the system records of the customer's orders, not from the customer's account of them.

## What counts toward a cap

| The customer's existing order of the same product is... | Counts toward items 1 to 3 | Can be the first order of a duplicate |
|---|---|---|
| submitted, processing or delivered | yes | yes |
| failed | yes | no |
| cancelled or refunded | no | no |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures, chosen for illustration)

**Destination cap.** Suppose a product's limit of orders to one destination in 24 hours is 3. In the last 24 hours the customer has placed three orders of that product to one phone number, one of which has since been refunded. Counting the new order and leaving out the refunded one gives 3, which is no more than 3: the order is within this cap. Had none of the three been cancelled or refunded, the count would be 4 and the order would not be placed.

**Value cap.** Suppose a product's 30-day value limit is $1000.00 and the customer's counted orders of that product in the last 30 calendar days total $950.00. A new order of $50.00 brings the total to exactly $1000.00, which is no more than the limit. A new order of $60.00 brings it to $1010.00, over the limit, and is not placed.

**Duplicate.** Suppose a product's duplicate window is 2 hours. A delivered order of $25.00 to a meter was placed at 09:00. A second order of the same product, the same meter and $25.00 placed at 10:30 is a duplicate and is not placed. A second order to the same meter at 10:30 for $30.00 is not of the same value, so the duplicate rule does not reach it; the caps in items 1 to 3 still apply to it. Had the 09:00 order been failed instead of delivered, it could not be the first order of a duplicate.
